prompt: Write a pull request description. Facts: the ingest worker retried a failed batch forever; one malformed row in the 03-03 file locked a Postgres partition for six hours on March 3rd and the on-call engineer drained the queue by hand; the fix caps attempts at three with backoff 1s/4s/16s and moves the batch to the ingest_dead_letter table; it closes issue 412; pytest tests/ingest passed 41 tests. Output only the PR description.
Write a pull request description for a one-line change. Facts: a typo in the CLI help text said 'recieve' instead of 'receive'; no behaviour change; no tests needed. Output only the PR description.

Write a git commit message (subject line and body). Facts: ingest batches now stop after three attempts instead of retrying forever, and move to the ingest_dead_letter table. Output only the commit message.

Write a Slack message to the #eng channel. Facts: the deploy is down for about 15 minutes; the ingest worker is stuck on a bad row in the 03-03 file; you are draining the queue now; you will post again when it clears. Output only the message.

Write a short Slack message to a teammate. Facts: you moved the weekly ingest sync from Wednesday to Thursday at 10am because half the team is out Wednesday; no action needed from them. Output only the message.

Write a release note entry. Facts: failed ingest batches now stop after three attempts instead of retrying forever; they move to the ingest_dead_letter table with their payload and last exception; replay them with bin/replay --batch-id <id>; requires Postgres 14 or newer. Output only the release note.

Write a runbook section titled 'Draining a stuck ingest partition'. Facts: symptom is ingest_lag_seconds above 3600 and one partition not advancing; check with bin/ingest status --partition <n>; the usual cause is a malformed row now sent to ingest_dead_letter; replay with bin/replay --batch-id <id>, which is idempotent; escalate to the data platform team if lag stays high for 30 minutes after replay. Output only the runbook section.

Write a short work email to Priya. Facts: you need the retry budget PR (#412) reviewed and merged by Friday or the March backfill slips; the worker retried one bad row for six hours on March 3rd; the fix caps attempts at three; you want her to confirm by Thursday. Output only the email.

Write the opening three paragraphs of a blog post about retry ceilings. Facts: on March 3rd an ingest worker spent six hours retrying one malformed row and held a Postgres partition, so the nightly backfill never ran; you wrote that retry loop two years earlier with backoff but no ceiling because you had only seen transient network failures, which always clear, and a malformed row never clears; the fix was four lines. Output only the paragraphs.

Write a LinkedIn post. Facts: an ingest worker you wrote two years ago retried one malformed row for six hours and held a Postgres partition; you had given the loop backoff but no ceiling; the fix was four lines, capping attempts at three and dead-lettering the batch. Output only the post.

Write a reply to a LinkedIn post that claims exponential backoff solves retry storms. Facts: backoff alone did not save you, because a malformed row never becomes valid, so the loop needs a ceiling and a dead-letter destination, not just longer waits. Output only the reply.

Write a code review comment. Facts: the function indexes rows[0] before it checks the length, so it raises on an empty list; the guard should move above line 42; this should block the merge. Output only the comment.

Write the code comment that should sit above the line `timeout = 30` in a client that calls a vendor API. Facts: the vendor's measured p99 latency was 22 seconds in August 2026; 30 seconds gives headroom; shorter timeouts caused spurious retries. Output only the comment, formatted as a Python comment.
